newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHIPYARD WORKERS TAKE VESSEL OUT OF ALBANIA.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHIPYARD WORKERS TAKE VESSEL OUT OF ALBANIA.

text.p: A group of 10 Polish workers left the north Albanian port of Durres on Thursday afternoon aboard a ship which was being repaired at a Polish-controlled shipyard there, their employer said.

Piotr Sojka, director of the Gdansk ship repair yard which owns 51 percent of the Durres yard, said the 10 had set out on the vessel Amber after Warsaw's foreign ministry advised the firm to evacuate its staff.
He told private Radio Zet they were headed for Dubrovnik in Croatia, adding: "They will get there if their fuel holds out. If not, they will pull in at a safe port."
Foreign Ministry spokesman Pawel Dobrowolski confirmed that Poland's embassy in Tirana had recommended evacuation.

"After consultation with the Polish embassy in Tirana, advice to leave Albania was given to 10 employees of the Gdansk ship repair yard who were working in Durres which is in the north of the country but where disturbances are starting," he said.
He added that embassy staff were remaining in Tirana but the ministry, which has set up a special crisis team to monitor Albania, was keeping in constant touch with them.
Anarchy has spread to the north of Albania following an anti-government uprising in the south sparked by anger over the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.
